item.title: Approve outbound license posture and upstream reuse strategy
item.deliverable: An approved decision record confirming Apache-2.0 for BPTK-authored material and covering BottleShip collaboration or fork posture, component license graph, provenance rule, and public naming review.
item.failure_meaning: BPTK cannot lawfully or coherently integrate upstream component or publish a runtime.
item.risk: A late license decision can force an architectural rewrite or prevent distribution.

item.title: Freeze a representative compatibility corpus
item.deliverable: A versioned corpus manifest of synthetic and redistributable fixture plus metadata-only user-title profile, stratified by API, architecture, era, and browser capability, with precommitted numeric correctness, startup, frame, audio, memory, variance, and sample threshold for every applicable scenario.
item.failure_meaning: Compatibility percentage and architecture choice have no stable denominator.
item.risk: A convenient but unrepresentative corpus can reward title-specific behavior and hide major gap.

item.title: Implement the benchmark runner and promotion gate
item.deliverable: A deterministic local and CI runner that executes live or temporary generated checks, retains no evidence artifact, enforces promotion metadata, and derives coverage count.
item.failure_meaning: Roadmap status can change without executable evidence or denominator reconciliation.
item.risk: Flaky browser artifact or mutable fixture would make promotion meaningless.

item.title: Approve the untrusted-import threat model
item.deliverable: A reviewed threat model for archive expansion, path traversal, parser memory, Wasm isolation, permission, network, storage, privacy, and hostile game code.
item.failure_meaning: The importer may expose local file, browser origin, network, or device resource to hostile input.
item.risk: An import-any-file UX creates a high-value parser and sandbox attack surface.

item.title: Complete the binary-runtime comparative spike
item.deliverable: A reproducible comparison of BottleShip adaptation, permissive component composition, and new implementation on the same PE32 fixture and browser profile.
item.failure_meaning: No binary architecture has demonstrated acceptable correctness, performance, license fit, and maintainability.
item.risk: Duplicating active prior art could consume the project before product differentiation is proven.

item.title: Complete the source-assisted pipeline spike
item.deliverable: A minimal C or C++ SDL and OpenGL game fixture compiled to Wasm, persisted, packaged, and run in the target browser profile.
item.failure_meaning: The source lane cannot produce a repeatable browser package from a representative native project.
item.risk: Toolchain success can hide application-level graphics, main-loop, file, thread, and network adaptation cost.

item.title: Build the safe importer and compatibility report
item.deliverable: A local-only inspector that classifies folder, archive, installer, PE, source tree, and engine asset into a lane or a specific blocked state without executing input.
item.failure_meaning: BPTK cannot uphold its minimum promise of accepting broad input and explaining what is required.
item.risk: Format ambiguity and hostile archive can cause unsafe parsing or misleading lane selection.

item.title: Implement PE32 loading and import resolution
item.deliverable: A bounded PE32 loader that maps section, relocation, import, TLS, stack, heap, and entry point for synthetic fixture.
item.failure_meaning: An eligible 32-bit executable cannot reach a deterministic entry point with a correct memory image.
item.risk: Malformed PE structure can produce memory corruption, unbounded allocation, or silent import mismatch.

item.title: Implement the i386 execution baseline
item.deliverable: An interpreter or selected upstream core that executes the frozen i386 instruction fixture with correct register, flag, FPU, exception, and memory result.
item.failure_meaning: Guest code diverges before operating-system API compatibility can be evaluated.
item.risk: Rare instruction, self-modifying code, FPU precision, and exception semantics can create deep title-specific failure.

item.title: Implement the Win32 core HLE
item.deliverable: A measured Kernel32, NTDLL, CRT, synchronization, time, process, thread-stub, memory, and COM baseline sufficient for the P1 fixture.
item.failure_meaning: Guest startup or main-loop control fails on an unimplemented or behaviorally incorrect core API.
item.risk: Windows behavior includes edge case and undocumented coupling that an API-name checklist will miss.

item.title: Implement USER32 window, message, and input behavior
item.deliverable: A deterministic window and message model mapped to canvas, keyboard, pointer, focus, cursor, timer, and browser lifecycle.
item.failure_meaning: The game cannot create a surface, pump a message loop, or receive reproducible input.
item.risk: Browser gesture, focus, shortcut, and asynchronous event rule differ substantially from Win32.

item.title: Implement the GDI compatibility slice
item.deliverable: A GDI surface supporting the corpus text, bitmap, palette, blit, clipping, brush, pen, font, and invalidation operation with image-golden output.
item.failure_meaning: Installer, launcher, menu, or software-rendered game output is missing or visually incorrect.
item.risk: Font and raster behavior vary by browser and platform and require controlled golden tolerance.

item.title: Implement DirectDraw surface and presentation
item.deliverable: A DirectDraw baseline for primary and offscreen surface, lock, blit, flip, palette, color key, pitch, and deterministic canvas presentation.
item.failure_meaning: A representative 2D game cannot render and present a correct frame.
item.risk: Legacy pixel format, pitch, palette, and timing behavior can differ from modern GPU surface.

item.title: Implement waveOut and DirectSound audio
item.deliverable: A WebAudio and AudioWorklet bridge for required PCM format, buffer, loop, volume, pan, timing, and lifecycle behavior.
item.failure_meaning: Audio is absent, corrupted, desynchronized, or blocks the guest main loop.
item.risk: Autoplay policy, callback timing, shared memory, sample conversion, and browser suspension can cause nondeterminism.

item.title: Implement file, registry, and OPFS overlay
item.deliverable: A case-aware virtual drive and registry with read-only base, copy-on-write save overlay, path normalization, quota behavior, and deterministic persistence.
item.failure_meaning: Game data, configuration, or save state is lost, exposed, aliased incorrectly, or written outside its sandbox.
item.risk: Windows path and case semantics, browser quota, transaction failure, and archive traversal can corrupt state.

item.title: Import the local package and prove the integrated 2D first playable
item.deliverable: A bounded importer for folder, ZIP, BPTK bundle, and explicitly supported installer format plus one integrated synthetic PE32 2D package that exercises loading, CPU, Win32, window, GDI, DirectDraw, audio, file, registry, save, input, and reload in one scenario.
item.failure_meaning: A supported package cannot be staged safely or the P1 component cannot operate together as one interactive, persistent 2D scenario.
item.risk: Archive failure or cross-component timing and lifecycle mismatch can pass isolated checks while the integrated package remains unusable.

item.title: Define WebGPU and WebGL2 capability profile
item.deliverable: A secure-context GPU probe and declared primary, fallback, degradation, limit, feature, format, and shader contract for each browser profile.
item.failure_meaning: Rendering code cannot distinguish a supported GPU path from a missing or partially compatible browser feature.
item.risk: WebGPU availability and limit vary across browser, operating system, driver, and hardware.

item.title: Translate Direct3D 7 and 8 fixed-function rendering
item.deliverable: A fixed-function state translator covering corpus transform, lighting, texture stage, blend, depth, fog, vertex format, draw, and presentation behavior.
item.failure_meaning: A representative early 3D fixture produces an incorrect frame or unsupported state without a precise report.
item.risk: State-combination explosion and implicit legacy default can cause shader-cache growth and subtle image divergence.

item.title: Translate Direct3D 9 fixed-function rendering
item.deliverable: A D3D9 fixed-function, resource, state block, render target, query-stub, and device-reset slice proven by image and API trace.
item.failure_meaning: A fixed-function D3D9 fixture cannot render correctly or recover from the declared device lifecycle.
item.risk: D3D9 caps, lost-device behavior, format conversion, and driver quirk exceed the simpler D3D7/8 model.

item.title: Translate Direct3D 9 shader model 1 through 3
item.deliverable: A validated translator from D3D9 tokenized vertex and pixel shader bytecode into the selected browser shader form with reflection, cache, error map, and golden output.
item.failure_meaning: A corpus shader is rejected, miscompiled, or renders outside the declared tolerance.
item.risk: Precision, undefined behavior, sampler model, shader limit, and backend difference can produce device-specific failure.

item.title: Publish the source-assisted adapter SDK
item.deliverable: A versioned Emscripten project adapter with main-loop, SDL, OpenGL, file, audio, input, build, patch, and diagnostic template for a representative source game.
item.failure_meaning: A developer cannot reproduce a source port without undocumented local step or bespoke host code.
item.risk: Build-system diversity and legacy dependency can turn a template into a misleading one-off.

item.title: Implement asset packaging, streaming, and cache
item.deliverable: A content-addressed package format with chunk, compression, integrity, lazy fetch, local cache, update, quota, and offline behavior.
item.failure_meaning: A legal large fixture cannot start within the size and time budget or cannot resume safely.
item.risk: Browser storage eviction, compression cost, cache poisoning, and monolithic asset can make a correct port unusable.

item.title: Meet the execution performance budget
item.deliverable: A profile-guided JIT or selected execution optimization, fast guest-host call path, cache policy, and frame-time budget on the frozen desktop fixture.
item.failure_meaning: Correct fixture cannot maintain its declared CPU, frame, audio, memory, and startup budget.
item.risk: Dynamic Wasm generation, browser compilation behavior, invalidation, and optimization complexity can trade correctness for speed.

item.title: Emit a framework-neutral browser package and React adapter
item.deliverable: A shared static package contract used by the integrated binary fixture and the source-assisted fixture, with canonical HTML canvas host, lifecycle API, capability report, worker and asset manifest, plus a thin React mount adapter.
item.failure_meaning: Binary and source output diverge into separate package contracts or cannot be embedded, resized, started, stopped, and deployed through both host forms.
item.risk: Host lifecycle, bundler, CSP, path, isolation header, and framework remount can corrupt runtime state.

item.title: Support the threaded deployment profile
item.deliverable: Separate threaded and single-thread package profile with COOP, COEP, worker pool, capability selection, and deterministic synchronization fixture.
item.failure_meaning: A thread-dependent port deadlocks, loses isolation, or silently runs the wrong build profile.
item.risk: Cross-origin resource, hosting configuration, browser worker limit, and main-thread proxy behavior can break deployment.

item.title: Implement the mediated network bridge
item.deliverable: A declared WebSocket, WebRTC, WebTransport, or optional proxy bridge with endpoint allowlist, consent, protocol adapter, latency metric, and offline failure.
item.failure_meaning: A network fixture cannot communicate through a browser-permitted transport with bounded security and latency.
item.risk: Raw TCP or UDP semantics, server compatibility, cheating, privacy, CORS, certificate, and relay cost cannot be hidden by a shim.

item.title: Complete controller, fullscreen, touch, and accessibility input
item.deliverable: A remappable input layer with keyboard, pointer lock, gamepad, fullscreen, touch control, focus recovery, accessible workbench UI, and browser-shortcut policy.
item.failure_meaning: A user cannot control, recover, or exit a packaged game reliably on the supported host profile.
item.risk: Gesture gating, browser-reserved shortcut, controller variance, mobile overlay, and accessibility conflict can make play unsafe or unusable.

item.title: Build the compatibility catalog and replay artifact
item.deliverable: A revisioned catalog with environment, input hash, capability, status, trace, replay, crash, screenshot, provenance, and community-observation state.
item.failure_meaning: Compatibility work cannot be reproduced, compared, diagnosed, or communicated truthfully.
item.risk: User asset privacy, personal data, nondeterminism, stale report, and title-version ambiguity can corrupt the catalog.

item.title: Publish the engine-family adapter contract
item.deliverable: A plugin contract for asset detector, version, local import, engine module, save, mod, input, network, package, license, and fixture, proven by one redistributable adapter.
item.failure_meaning: An engine-specific port requires a one-off workbench and cannot share BPTK packaging or evidence.
item.risk: An adapter can accidentally imply right to game asset or fragment the core with title-specific behavior.

item.title: Pass the cross-browser and device matrix
item.deliverable: A declared Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari desktop matrix with selected mobile probe, GPU profile, degradation rule, artifact, and support floor.
item.failure_meaning: A package labeled supported behaves differently or fails silently on a declared browser or device profile.
item.risk: WebGPU rollout, codec, storage, input, memory, isolation, and driver behavior can differ despite shared web standard.

item.title: Research the x86-64 and memory64 path
item.deliverable: A measured architecture decision for x86-64 execution, address space, Wasm memory64 or segmentation, browser support, JIT, exception, and performance with a promotion proposal.
item.failure_meaning: There is no evidenced browser architecture for 64-bit Windows game within the supported memory and performance envelope.
item.risk: Pointer width, address-space reservation, browser memory limit, JIT design, and missing upstream CPU feature can invalidate the PE32 architecture.

item.title: Research Direct3D 10 and 11 translation
item.deliverable: A feature-gap and prototype report for DXGI, D3D10/11, DXBC, resource model, shader translation, synchronization, and WebGPU limit on a bounded fixture.
item.failure_meaning: The modern graphics feature set cannot be mapped to WebGPU with acceptable correctness and performance.
item.risk: DXVK behavior assumes Vulkan feature and native driver control that WebGPU intentionally abstracts or omits.

item.title: Research Direct3D 12 and Vulkan-era compatibility
item.deliverable: A no-marketing feasibility report comparing D3D12 and Vulkan requirement to current WebGPU, shader, descriptor, synchronization, memory, x86-64, and browser capability.
item.failure_meaning: Modern API compatibility lacks a credible mapping or depends on browser feature outside the declared horizon.
item.risk: The gap can remain architectural rather than an implementation backlog, making broad modern-game support uneconomic.

item.title: Bridge blocking Win32 and synchronous storage over async browser API
item.deliverable: A JS Promise Integration call bridge that services blocking Win32 wait, sleep, and synchronous file and OPFS access over asynchronous browser API, with a feature-detected Asyncify fallback where JSPI is unavailable.
item.failure_meaning: A supported blocking Win32 or synchronous storage call cannot complete in the browser without whole-module instrumentation, or diverges between the JSPI and fallback path.
item.risk: Synchronous game code stalls, deadlocks, or corrupts state when a blocking call is serviced incorrectly across the async boundary.

item.title: Adopt a WebAssembly 3.0 execution substrate for the i386 engine
item.deliverable: An i386 execution substrate that uses WebAssembly tail-call dispatch, exnref exception handling, and relaxed SIMD where available, with strict-SIMD and legacy exception fallback for a browser that lacks them.
item.failure_meaning: The engine cannot dispatch a translated block, unwind a guest exception, or execute packed SIMD without wasm-stack growth or a portability regression across the declared browser set.
item.risk: A substrate that assumes one browser feature set silently loses correctness or performance where that feature is flagged or absent.

item.title: Learn whether per-title static recompilation to WebAssembly is a viable fourth lane
item.deliverable: A no-marketing feasibility report evaluating static machine-code to C or C++ to WebAssembly recompilation, in the N64Recomp, PSXRecomp, and XenonRecomp tradition, as a distinct lane for a title the general high-level-emulation binary lane cannot reach when source or a clean recompilation exists.
item.failure_meaning: The static-recompilation lane lacks a credible per-title pipeline, a legal input path, or a measured advantage over the existing binary and source lane.
item.risk: A speculative fourth lane consumes roadmap capacity without a title that only it can reach.

item.title: Classify known game middleware and copy protection to route handle, warn, extract, or refuse
item.deliverable: A static pre-flight census that detects a known middleware and copy-protection signal from PE import, section, overlay, and sibling-file evidence across video, audio, installer, and protection component, and returns a handle, warn, extract, or refuse routing decision without executing the input or circumventing any protection.
item.failure_meaning: A supported title is mis-routed, so a portable middleware path is refused or a copy-protected or unsupported binary is accepted as portable.
item.risk: A false portable decision wastes downstream lane effort, and a false refuse hides a title that would run.

item.title: Extract a supported installer to the game payload without executing it
item.deliverable: A client-side extractor that unpacks a supported Inno Setup, GOG, or InstallShield cabinet installer to the game payload, refuses a 16-bit setup stub, and never runs installer code.
item.failure_meaning: A supported installer cannot be unpacked to a usable payload, or installer code is executed instead of extracted.
item.risk: Running an installer stub executes untrusted code, and a failed extraction blocks a title whose payload is otherwise portable.

item.title: Serve every guest time source from one monotonic clock
item.deliverable: A timing layer that derives QueryPerformanceCounter, RDTSC, GetTickCount, timeGetTime, vertical-blank, and frame timing from a single monotonic source, honors the one-millisecond period expectation, and clamps a delta so a guest neither busy-spins nor runs at double speed.
item.failure_meaning: Guest timing diverges across the clock source, so the game slows, double-speeds, or busy-waits at full utilization.
item.risk: A per-call clock choice desynchronizes physics, animation, and audio from the frame.

item.title: Play supported full-motion-video middleware in sync with the game
item.deliverable: A video path that decodes a supported Bink, Smacker, and VP6 full-motion video and presents it through the browser frame and audio, while refusing a proprietary WMV or Indeo bitstream that cannot be decoded lawfully.
item.failure_meaning: A supported cutscene cannot decode or present in sync, or an unsupported proprietary bitstream is accepted.
item.risk: A missing or out-of-sync cutscene path blocks progression or desynchronizes video from audio.

item.title: Provide the redistributable runtime a supported game expects
item.deliverable: A redistributable kit that satisfies a supported game's exact D3DX, XInput, XAudio, Visual C++ runtime, Visual Basic 6 runtime, and DirectMusic instrument dependency, ships only a redistributable component, and reports an unmet dependency rather than faking it.
item.failure_meaning: A supported game exits because an expected redistributable runtime component is missing or wrongly versioned.
item.risk: Bundling a non-redistributable component creates a license violation, while omitting one blocks an otherwise portable title.

item.title: Build a game source tree to the browser with a pinned Emscripten profile
item.deliverable: A committed, reproducible Emscripten build profile for the source lane that sets cross-origin isolation, pthreads with SharedArrayBuffer, native WebAssembly exception, relaxed SIMD with fallback, and a WASMFS OPFS backend driven by JSPI rather than legacy Asyncify, and produces a deterministic module from a supported source tree.
item.failure_meaning: A supported source tree cannot build to a working browser module under the pinned profile, or the build is not reproducible.
item.risk: An unpinned build silently selects legacy Asyncify or drops isolation and ships a broken or non-reproducible module.

item.title: Route a supported game to a matching open engine reimplementation
item.deliverable: An engine-family census that fingerprints a supported game engine from executable and asset signal and routes it to a matching browser-capable open reimplementation under the adapter contract, or reports no match, without bundling engine or game code.
item.failure_meaning: A supported game is routed to the wrong open engine, or a matchable game reports no match.
item.risk: A wrong engine match wastes adapter effort and misleads the compatibility decision.

item.title: Bound extraction, streaming, and execution against resource exhaustion
item.deliverable: A bounded-resource enforcement layer that caps decompressed output size, nesting depth, and expansion ratio during installer extraction and asset streaming, guards the OPFS quota, and enforces a memory and time budget on guest execution, refusing input that exceeds a declared bound.
item.failure_meaning: A crafted archive, asset stream, or guest program exhausts memory, storage, or time instead of being refused at a declared bound.
item.risk: An unbounded extraction or execution path is a denial-of-service and quota-exhaustion vector against the user's browser.

item.title: Contain guest execution to a policy that cannot reach host capability
item.deliverable: A guest containment policy that confines executed game code to WebAssembly memory, a content-security policy without arbitrary host script, storage limited to the package OPFS sandbox, and network only through the mediated relay, and refuses any escape attempt.
item.failure_meaning: Executed guest code reaches a host capability such as arbitrary script, storage outside its sandbox, or unmediated network, outside the declared policy.
item.risk: A containment gap turns an imported game into a host-compromise or data-exfiltration vector.

item.title: Recompile PE32 machine code ahead of time to WebAssembly
item.deliverable: An ahead-of-time translator that lowers supported i386 `.text` of a mapped PE32 image to WebAssembly module, plus a run lane that executes the emitted module under the declared containment policy with the interpreter oracle as reference.
item.failure_meaning: Guest execution stays interpreter-bound and the performance thesis of the roadmap stays unproven.
item.risk: A translator optimized for speed over exactness silently diverges from the oracle and corrupts state in an unrelated subsystem.

item.title: Recover control flow and indirect branch target
item.deliverable: A control-flow recovery pass that reconstructs function boundary, jump table, and vtable target from the mapped image and feeds the recompiler, with declared fallback for unknown target and flagged code-as-data region.
item.failure_meaning: The recompiler is limited to straight-line code and cannot serve real game dispatch.
item.risk: A recovered target that is actually data produces a corrupt recompiled branch that only fails deep in a game.

item.title: Fall back to interpretation for self-modifying code
item.deliverable: A hybrid execution policy that detects writes into recompiled page, invalidates and re-decodes the affected block, and keeps untouched block on the recompiled path.
item.failure_meaning: Game that patch their own code or emit code at runtime execute stale instruction and crash or corrupt.
item.risk: An overly broad invalidation erases the performance advantage; an overly narrow one executes stale code.

item.title: Research x86-64 recompilation feasibility
item.deliverable: A bounded feasibility report plus a prototype that recompiles a 64-bit research fixture and compares 64-bit GPR, RIP-relative, and SSE-default behavior against an x64 reference.
item.failure_meaning: The modern-PC lane stays a deferral without evidence for or against 64-bit recompilation.
item.risk: A 64-bit prototype that ignores exception and address-space difference overstates feasibility.

item.title: Serve a memory64 guest address space
item.deliverable: A memory64-backed guest address space for the execution substrate with declared trap behavior for out-of-bounds access.
item.failure_meaning: Guest code that relies on large or sparse address space cannot run, or wraps into unrelated memory.
item.risk: A browser without memory64 support needs a declared fallback or an honest block.

item.title: Run guest thread on a worker pool
item.deliverable: A guest-thread layer that maps guest thread onto a worker pool over SharedArrayBuffer with deterministic lock, atomic, and scheduling behavior under the declared containment policy.
item.failure_meaning: Threaded game cannot run or deadlock nondeterministically.
item.risk: Worker scheduling leaks into guest-visible behavior and breaks determinism that record and replay depends on.

item.title: Execute packed SIMD and 80-bit x87 exactly
item.deliverable: A SIMD and x87 execution layer covering the declared packed and 80-bit subset with declared tolerance, plus a strict fallback path for host without the assumed feature.
item.failure_meaning: Game math that depends on packed or extended-precision behavior diverges silently.
item.risk: A tolerance chosen after seeing results hides real divergence.

item.title: Dispatch structured exception and TLS callback
item.deliverable: An exception and callback layer that serves structured and vectored exception behavior over the substrate exception mechanism and runs TLS callback in declared order before guest entry.
item.failure_meaning: Game that rely on exception-based control flow or TLS initialization crash or skip initialization.
item.risk: Exception delivery that skips cleanup corrupts guest state silently.

item.title: Satisfy benign anti-debug and timing check
item.deliverable: A guard-satisfaction layer that answers benign debugger-presence and timing query with declared values and keeps the census refusal for protection intact.
item.failure_meaning: Benignly protected title stay blocked or, worse, protection gets bypassed.
item.risk: The same mechanism that satisfies a benign check can be tuned into a protection bypass.

item.title: Record and replay a CPU-deterministic run
item.deliverable: A record-and-replay layer that captures the declared nondeterminism source and replays them to an identical guest state hash locally and on a second machine.
item.failure_meaning: Compatibility evidence and divergence diagnosis lose their reproducibility foundation.
item.risk: A replay that misses one nondeterminism source hashes identically today and diverges tomorrow.

item.title: Lower guest import call to host emulation
item.deliverable: An ABI lowering pass that turns recompiled import call into direct host-emulation call with per-calling-convention stack cleanup and a measured boundary cost.
item.failure_meaning: Recompiled code cannot reach Win32 emulation and the recompiler stays a laboratory artifact.
item.risk: A boundary cost above the declared bar erases the recompiler performance advantage.

item.title: Research the PowerPC console lane
item.deliverable: A bounded feasibility report plus a prototype that recompiles a PowerPC research fixture and compares behavior against a reference, with the Xenon desktop-only prior-art result recorded.
item.failure_meaning: The console lane stays a name without evidence for or against it.
item.risk: Console-specific hardware assumption leak into a prototype that then overstates feasibility.

item.title: Research the MIPS console lane and PS2 gap
item.deliverable: A bounded spike that recompiles MIPS research fixture against a reference emulator trace and records the PS2 VU/GS gap as pinned or deferred.
item.failure_meaning: The older console lane stays unevaluated.
item.risk: A partial MIPS result is generalized into a support claim.

item.title: Lower every shader frontend to one unified intermediate representation
item.deliverable: A unified shader intermediate representation with a single WGSL emitter, plus a static audit that fails when a second emitter appears in the tree.
item.failure_meaning: The known three-emitter drift reproduces and identical game state renders differently per frontend.
item.risk: An emitter added for convenience outside the audit scope silently reintroduces the drift.

item.title: Research the DXBC and DXIL frontend
item.deliverable: A bounded research report plus a prototype reader over the DXVK, dxil-spirv, SPIR-V, and Tint prior-art chain that names unsupported opcode explicitly.
item.failure_meaning: The modern shader lane stays unevaluated or quietly drops instruction.
item.risk: A dropped opcode renders wrong output that looks plausible.

item.title: Lower Direct3D 9 shader-model 1 through 3 to the unified representation
item.deliverable: A Direct3D 9 shader-model frontend over the unified representation that replaces any standalone emitter for the declared corpus.
item.failure_meaning: Shader-model content renders through a divergent path and the unified-representation promise is void.
item.risk: Byte-identical output is relaxed for one opcode and the drift begins again.

item.title: Research the OpenGL and Glide shader frontend
item.deliverable: An OpenGL, ARB assembly, and Glide frontend over the unified representation serving the declared combiner subset.
item.failure_meaning: GL-era and Glide-era title lack a translation path.
item.risk: A combiner approximation outside the declared tolerance silently shifts color or blending.

item.title: Compile the fixed-function pipeline once
item.deliverable: One fixed-function pipeline generator covering the declared light, texture-stage-operation, fog, and alpha matrix, consumed by every fixed-function frontend.
item.failure_meaning: Fixed-function content renders per-API instead of per-state and compatibility evidence splits.
item.risk: A generator parameter tuned for one API shifts another API's output.

item.title: Verify texgen, projective, and shadow-cookie correctness
item.deliverable: Texgen, projective mapping, and shadow-cookie correctness over the fixed-function generator, with the named projection-divide regression covered fail-closed.
item.failure_meaning: The named silent-wrong-shadow bug class reproduces.
item.risk: A tolerance wide enough to pass a missing divide hides the exact named bug.

item.title: Report capability honestly against translator support
item.deliverable: A capability report bound to measured translator support, with a by-construction failure when advertisement exceeds support.
item.failure_meaning: The known advertise-more-than-implemented defect reproduces at the product surface.
item.risk: The report reads support from configuration instead of the compiled translator.

item.title: Regress rendered frames against a reference computed at test time
item.deliverable: A frame-diff regression check that computes its reference at test time over the declared metric set and retains no baseline artifact.
item.failure_meaning: Silent rendering drift ships because no frame comparison guards the pipeline.
item.risk: A reference generated from the implementation under test compares against itself and sees nothing.

item.title: Serve the WebGPU primary backend from the unified representation
item.deliverable: The primary representation-to-WGSL backend serving the full declared fixture set on a live adapter.
item.failure_meaning: The primary GPU path cannot carry the compatibility corpus.
item.risk: A backend validated only on synthetic happy-path fixture misses real state combination.

item.title: Serve the WebGL2 fallback from the unified representation
item.deliverable: A representation-to-GLSL-ES fallback backend with the declared tolerance floor and named blocking above it.
item.failure_meaning: Host without WebGPU get no honest path or a silent wrong one.
item.risk: The looser tolerance drifts into hiding real divergence.

item.title: Serve the WebGPU compatibility-mode backend
item.deliverable: A compatibility-mode backend targeting the declared feature level with emit-time subset enforcement.
item.failure_meaning: Older GPU class stay locked out of the primary path.
item.risk: Subset enforcement that reads the wrong feature level passes out-of-subset output.

item.title: Present frames with correct gamma, dirty rect, and pacing
item.deliverable: A presentation layer covering swapchain, gamma, dirty-rect, and present pacing semantics over the browser surface.
item.failure_meaning: Every rendered frame is subtly wrong or slower than budget.
item.risk: Gamma measured only at endpoints misses the mid-gray error.

item.title: Resolve multisample and convert surface format
item.deliverable: A multisample resolve and format-conversion layer with declared fallback and reporting for unsupported sample count.
item.failure_meaning: Multisampled title render aliased or wrong-format without explanation.
item.risk: A silent fallback to one sample is indistinguishable from a correct resolve in a green suite.

item.title: Research console framebuffer and embedded-memory resolve
item.deliverable: A bounded feasibility report with a prototype of the embedded-memory tile-resolve-to-WebGPU mapping.
item.failure_meaning: The console framebuffer lane stays unevaluated.
item.risk: A prototype measured only on desktop GPU overstates portable feasibility.

item.title: Research compute and modern shader support
item.deliverable: A bounded research report with a compute prototype and the declared above-limit blocking matrix.
item.failure_meaning: Modern compute content stays unevaluated.
item.risk: A bit-identical claim measured on one adapter set overstates portability.

item.title: Contain hostile shader bytecode in the translator
item.deliverable: A translator containment layer that bounds time and memory for hostile bytecode and fails closed with a structured reason.
item.failure_meaning: The DarthShader bug class reaches the runtime through imported shader bytecode.
item.risk: A bound measured on a small fuzz set misses the deeper recursion or expansion case.

item.title: Cache compiled pipeline by content address
item.deliverable: A content-addressed pipeline and shader cache integrated with packaging, with precise invalidation on input change.
item.failure_meaning: Every launch pays full compile cost or, worse, serves stale pipeline.
item.risk: An under-hashed key reuses stale pipeline after a game update.

item.title: Keep a clonable, non-stale repository with a reproducible release
item.deliverable: A release process and CI gate that keeps a clean clone green, fails a stale default branch at the declared window, and reproduces a release artifact from its tag.
item.failure_meaning: The known seven-week-stale-branch defect reproduces and every claim loses its verifiable baseline.
item.risk: A freshness window set loosely enough to survive neglect hides the exact failure it exists to catch.

item.title: Run a public issue and compatibility tracker
item.deliverable: Public issue and compatibility tracker templates that reject a bare report and a triage-freshness service level for accepted report.
item.failure_meaning: The known empty-tracker defect reproduces and compatibility knowledge stays private.
item.risk: A template that accepts a bare report accumulates unusable entries that poison triage.

item.title: Publish the compatibility database export
item.deliverable: A published compatibility database export with byte-stable format and refusal of unbacked or personal-data row.
item.failure_meaning: Published compatibility claim has no evidence backing or leaks personal data.
item.risk: An export that drifts byte-wise between revision breaks every downstream consumer silently.

item.title: Enforce the test-first and ratcheting coverage bar
item.deliverable: A gate rule that links every runtime surface to a benchmark and ratchets coverage on runtime module against a frozen floor.
item.failure_meaning: The known roughly-ten-percent-test defect reproduces on every new surface.
item.risk: A floor set below the current state lets coverage decay while the gate stays green.

item.title: Remove the single-maintainer bus factor
item.deliverable: A maintainer record, code-owner rule, two-signer release requirement, and a documented recovery drill.
item.failure_meaning: The known bus-factor-one defect reproduces and the project dies with its maintainer.
item.risk: A recovery path that exists only in prose is untestable and therefore absent when needed.

item.title: Accept human and agent contribution through one gate
item.deliverable: A contributor pipeline where agent and human authorship is disclosed and the full gate applies identically.
item.failure_meaning: Agent contribution bypasses the evidence bar or hides authorship.
item.risk: A disclosure rule without enforcement decays into convention.

item.title: Resolve the license, reuse, and provenance graph
item.deliverable: A license, reuse, and provenance graph that binds every component and hosted title to its decision record and fails closed on an unlicensed, incompatible, or expired node.
item.failure_meaning: Publication decisions rest on ad-hoc review instead of a resolvable graph.
item.risk: A graph that trusts a stale node publishes under an expired grant.

item.title: Govern breaking change and analytics honestly
item.deliverable: A governance rule binding breaking change to a merged decision record and a byte-level audit that analytics stay aggregate and opt-in, with community space recorded.
item.failure_meaning: Breaking change ship silently and analytics trust cannot be verified.
item.risk: An analytics audit that samples instead of auditing byte flow misses a leak.
